scope: Real TLS 1.2 / WebSocket transport boundary on ESP32 against a host adversarial peer; no Sonos discovery or playback commands.
execution: Parent operated hardware and captured logs; independent reviewer inspected completed logs. This record does not certify the current flashed production image.

fixture.trust: Ephemeral private CA; hostname-verified leaf SAN matches host IP. Private keys excluded from this record.

timing_contract.internal_origin: First gate_read after deadline reset; reads of the same frame share that deadline. Completed-frame callbacks reset it.
timing_contract.outer_origin: Host monotonic time immediately before sending initial attack bytes; ends on observed peer EOF/reset or failed socket write.
timing_contract.revision: Review revised the experimental outer criterion; the production internal timeout is unchanged. original strict five-second failures remain failures. Existing oversized-control and trickle-frame runs are separately assessed against six seconds without rewriting their peer verdicts.
timing_contract.justification: A five-second receive deadline starts on the device, later than host send. Delivery, task scheduling, timer granularity, shutdown, and return-path observation add latency. Six seconds is an outer acceptance limit for these runs, not a proven latency bound.
timing_contract.clock_limit: Host monotonic and UART device-uptime clocks are not synchronized. Exact first gate_read timestamps were not logged; do not subtract host timestamps from UART timestamps.

uart_crosscheck.interpretation: Consistent with five-second receive timeout plus scheduling; header rejection is not the exact deadline origin.

timing_contract.zero_ms_drop: Reported integer-millisecond duration, not proof of literally zero execution time.

explicit_cancellation.interpretation: During an incomplete TLS record, the owning worker entered Socket Drop at its cancellation timer; cancellation released the receive task and destruction returned in a reported 26 ms. Host closure occurred 1.8377 seconds after attack start. The two time origins are distinct.
explicit_cancellation.coverage_limit: One explicit cancellation run with partial TLS; no explicit-cancel run for oversized-control or trickle-frame. No general real-time bound claimed.

limitations: Single completed automatic run per attack, not endurance or repeated-connect leak proof.
Each successful automatic run reports 1208 fewer internal free bytes after destruction than before connect; attribution and repeated-run stability were not established.
Partial TLS retry includes stock transport esp_tls_conn_read error logs during incomplete-record reads; retain them as evidence, not a clean-log claim.
Connect and write worst-case deadlines, stack margin, and normal playback are outside this fixture acceptance.
Raw logs and ELFs are ignored target artifacts; selected evidence and their hashes are retained here.
acceptance_summary: Three automatic attack cases satisfy the revised six-second outer criterion after valid baselines; explicit cancellation during partial TLS returned from Drop in 26 ms and execution continued. Preserve the two original strict-five-second failures and initial partial-TLS pre-baseline connection failure.
